name: plain-removal
prompt:
Players can place blocks but can't take them back. Let them remove blocks they placed: right-click a block on PC, or long-press it on a phone or tablet. Only the player who placed a block can remove it, and removing needs the same server-side checks as placing (reach and rate).

Placement is in src/ServerScriptService/BlockPlacement.server.luau and src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/BlockPlacer.luau.

checks.text: No module loader, LOAD_MODULE tags, or new ServerScriptService/Modules tree is introduced in a project that doesn't use them

rubric: Fits the project as it is: the feature goes into the existing placement script and client module (plus a shared module in ReplicatedStorage/Shared if one helps), in their style. The attempt doesn't bring in a framework or code layout the project doesn't use (a module loader, Init/Start services, a new folder tree) and doesn't move, rename, or restructure the existing scripts.

Ownership is enforced on the server: the server records who placed each block (an attribute or a server-side table keyed by part) and refuses removal requests from anyone else; nothing the client sends is trusted for this.

Removal requests are validated like placement: the target must be an Instance that is a block in the Blocks folder (checked with typeof, IsA, and IsDescendantOf or similar), within reach of the character, and rate-limited, and the occupied-cell record is cleared so the cell can be built on again.
Input: right-click removes on PC and a long press removes on touch, without breaking click or tap to place, and input already processed by UI is ignored.

Correct and in scope: placement keeps working, changes stay in the placement files plus anything strictly needed, and luau-lsp, selene, and StyLua pass on the changed files. Supporting files such as stories or specs count neither for nor against.
